| Value of `text` | Question to answer first | What the caller would see under the other answer | Decision in contract R05 (fixed in advance) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `null` | No message, or a format error? | If treated as an error, a stream that should report "completed without an agent message" (5) reports malformed (6) instead | No message: nothing is printed and nothing counts as spoken |
| `false`, `0` | No message, like `null`, or a type error? | If treated as no message, the caller learns only "completed without an agent message" when upstream sent the wrong type | Malformed: emit one diagnostic and continue with the next line |
| `123` | May a number be printed as review content? | Under the old behavior, the caller receives exit 0 and believes it has a review | Malformed |
| `" "` (whitespace only) | Does whitespace count as content? Should it be stripped? | If stripped, a message the old caller used to receive disappears; if it was the only message, the result moves from 0 to 5 | Valid: printed unchanged and counted as one spoken message |

| Content | Question it answers | After deleting it | Who confirms |
|---|---|---|---|
| Undecided requirement | Does the team not yet know which behavior to accept? | There is no decision to delete; writing it as a requirement means guessing the owner's answer | The owner of the requirement, the interface or the compatibility obligation |
| Normative requirement | What must the delivered program do, and what must it avoid? | If it was the sole basis, the legal set changes; a duplicated clause may not | The spec owner and the affected callers |
| Rationale | Why was it decided this way, and where is it easy to misread? | The legal set is unchanged; readers lose their basis for judging exceptions | The spec owner and maintainers |
| Example | What does the rule look like applied to a concrete input? | The legal set is unchanged; the rule's meaning is harder to confirm | The spec owner and the QA owner |
| Self-check | Which easily missed requirement should the implementer recheck before submitting the candidate? | The legal set is unchanged; one reminder pointing back to the clause is lost | The implementer and whoever is responsible for acceptance |
| Optional pattern | How might the implementation be arranged? | The legal set is unchanged; one suggested path is lost | The implementer, with help from the architecture owner when needed |

| Observation point | Contract requires | Hypothetical candidate |
|---|---|---|
| stdout | One blank line, then `<!-- tokens: in 12 out 3 -->` | The same |
| stderr | `[codex malformed event] line 1:` followed by a nonempty reason | No malformed diagnostic; instead, `[codex] the turn completed without an agent message; no review was produced.` is appended at the end |
| exit | 6 | 5 |

| Observed phenomenon | Necessary premises | Judgment available | Next step and owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Two candidates behave differently on the same input, and both behaviors are defensible | Whether the spec has an explicit answer for this input; whether callers already depend on one of the behaviors | If there is no answer: undecided requirement | The requirements or interface owner decides and records it; expected values that depend on this policy stay unsettled |
| A candidate violates an explicit requirement, for example by skipping `false` | Reproducible with a minimal input; candidate, spec and acceptance versions match; acceptance has been checked with positive and negative controls | The implementation did not meet a settled requirement; the cause is unknown | Reject the candidate; to change the document, write a separate change card stating the hypothesis |
| Acceptance rejects an output that looks legal, for example because the REASON is worded differently | Whether the contract allows this variation | The yardstick is stricter than the contract | The QA owner fixes the oracle, keeps the old scores, and re-scores existing artifacts consistently |
| Two documents say what looks like the same thing, but allow different things | A candidate can be found that is legal under one and illegal under the other | The requirements are inconsistent, or one document changed the scope | The spec owner aligns the requirements in a new version, without modifying the frozen packet |
| A candidate follows the optional pattern but violates its exception (hypothetical: applying the strict text helper to the top-level error) | Whether the optional pattern is marked optional and states its exception | The implementation violates the contract; the pattern's wording may be risky | Reject the candidate; check that the exception is written next to the corresponding requirement |

| Intervention | Gap it addresses | Concrete action | Main owner | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Spec exploration | Nobody has decided the behavior yet | List the questions and examples, hand them to the owner to decide and record | The requirements or interface owner | Settled requirements need not pretend to be under exploration; concrete examples can still check understanding |
| Text intervention: rationale, example, self-check, optional pattern | A decided requirement may be misread or overlooked | Write a change card, change one category at a time, and connect it to acceptance and a comparison | The spec owner and the QA owner | While the requirement is undecided, the text is only guessing the answer on someone's behalf |
| Executable feedback | Can the agent detect errors in its candidate before delivery? | Turn mechanically decidable requirements into executable checks that the agent can run in its environment or that external acceptance applies | QA and the platform owner | When the model cannot use tools, no execution feedback is available within the session; external acceptance is still useful. The checks themselves also need positive and negative controls |

| Document | Main content | Mix-ups to avoid | Owner and review timing |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standing guidance (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, constitution) | Ways of working that hold across tasks, such as verification commands and areas that must not be changed | Treating a one-off choice or an undecided policy as a settled cross-task rule | The repo or platform owner; on adding text, state which requirement it serves and which error it aims to reduce; review periodically, and immediately on a conflict |
| One-off spec | The requirements this change alters, the compatibility scope, what is out of scope, and open questions | Presenting a new project-wide rule as a requirement that applies only this time; existing general rules may be cited | The task's requirements owner; when the task ends, decide which content is promoted and which is archived with the task |
| Continuously maintained spec | Behavior callers depend on and that must hold across versions, such as the exit precedence and the legacy diagnostic strings | Writing an accidental implementation detail, or a reminder that serves only this task, as a long-term obligation; necessary architectural constraints may be listed explicitly | The interface owner; review when the requirements are revised, a caller retires, or acceptance is revised |
